does: Cuts sheets of warqa into long strips, puts a spoonful of filling at one end of each strip and folds the end over it again and again, corner to corner, into a small neat triangle, with the loose end sealed down with a dab of fat.

intro.what: Warqa strips wrap a filling in repeated corner-to-corner folds that make a neat triangle.
intro.why: Keeping the pastry supple and the filling restrained lets the thin sheet close without cracks or exposed corners.

how: Keep the warqa under a damp cloth. Cut a sheet into strips as wide as a hand, and brush each strip lightly with melted butter.
Put a small spoonful of filling at one end, a little in from the corner.
Fold the corner over the filling to make a triangle, then fold the triangle over on itself along the strip, again and again, as one folds a flag.
Seal the last flap with a dab of butter and tuck it under.
Lay the triangles on a tray and cover them until they are fried.

cues.text: Each pastry is a neat triangle with no filling showing at the corners.
The sealed flap holds without sticking and the triangle is firm and flat.

mistakes.mistake: Overfilling, which splits the thin sheet and leaks in the oil.
Letting the strips dry out, so that they crack when folded.
mistakes.fix: Cut only a few at a time and keep the rest under a damp cloth.

quiz.question: Why keep unused warqa strips under a damp cloth?
choices: To prevent drying that causes cracks during folding.
To dry the surfaces so the folds hold their corners.
To make the pastry soak up extra filling moisture.
quiz.because: Supple warqa can fold around the filling without snapping.

quiz.question: How is the triangle carried along the strip?
choices: Roll the strip into an open cylinder.
Fold it corner to corner repeatedly along the strip.
Gather the strip into loose pleats above the filling.
quiz.because: The repeated diagonal folds enclose the filling within the triangular shape.

quiz.question: What should the finished briouat look like?
choices: A loose strip with filling exposed at each end.
A split parcel with a thick mound pushing through.
A neat triangle with filling enclosed at the corners.
quiz.because: Enclosed corners and a secured flap show the wrapper has closed around the filling.

quiz.question: The warqa split around an overfilled centre. What would you change on the next parcel?
choices: Use less filling so the folds can close.
Pack more filling against the split.
Stretch the dry strip harder across the mound.
quiz.because: Reducing the filling relieves pressure on the thin wrapper.

variant_of.differs: Wrapping encloses a filling in a leaf, caul fat or a thin omelette. Here the wrapper is a paper-thin sheet cut in strips, and the filling is folded up in a series of triangle folds along the strip.
